correctness.rationale: For the explicitly bounded self-adjoint two-sided diamond Hamiltonian, the second and third transfer moments to an adjacent hub are respectively \(S_j\) and \((v_j+v_{j+1})S_j+T_j\). Complete confinement forces both zero; with all path couplings nonzero this implies equal arm energies. Conversely, equal energies plus orthogonality of the two complex vectors give a sitewise orthogonal rotation and an exact direct sum of irreducible 3-by-3 Jacobi matrices for the entire infinite chain. Taylor expansion proves leading leakage coefficients at order \(t^4\) with coefficient \(|S_j|^2/4\), or order \(t^6\) with coefficient \(|\overline{r_U}\ell_U|^2|\epsilon_U-\epsilon_V|^2/36\); both vanish identically under block splitting. A seeded 3378-group numerical and symbolic checker was executed. Tests are not an infinite proof, and the spectrum is correctly specified as the closure of the block eigenvalues.

value.rationale: Aharonov–Bohm caging is sensitive to imperfections, and previous disorder studies distinguish onsite and bond disorder. This theorem gives a sharp gauge-invariant, locally enforceable criterion to preserve every hub cage across arbitrary bounded spatial variation, not just a single fixed-energy flat band, and a complete localized spectral decomposition. Independent failure mechanisms have distinct leading measurable adjacent-hub leakage probabilities, quartic for interference failure and sextic for arm-energy imbalance. The classification is a meaningful structural design and diagnostic result; it does not rely on a tiny numerical gain or isolated arbitrary parameter choice.
